tagline: The best view of Manhattan isn't in Manhattan.
neighborhood: Hunters Point, Long Island City — one block from the East River
positioning: The Larkin is a 34-story, 318-residence tower at the corner of 46th Avenue and 5th Street in Hunters Point — one block from the East River, two blocks from the 7 at Vernon Blvd-Jackson Ave, and one stop from Grand Central. Completed in 2023 by Halbrook Property Group, it is built around a single idea: the best view of Manhattan is the one you get from across the river. Twenty-nine residential floors are stacked so that nearly every home takes a western or northern exposure — the skyline, the Queensboro Bridge, the ferries working the East River — and 26,000 square feet of amenities on three levels are turned the same way: The Works on three, The Terrace and its 62-foot pool on four, The Overlook on thirty-four. The Larkin does not sell escape from the city. It sells the best seat in the house.
brandVoice: Second person, present tense, plainspoken. Short declarative sentences, at most one em-dash aside per paragraph. Every claim is quantified or named: square feet, floor numbers, minutes to Grand Central, the actual name of the restaurant on the corner (Casa Enrique, Sweetleaf, LIC Landing, Gantry Plaza State Park, MoMA PS1, The Noguchi Museum). Homes are 'residences,' never 'units.' Amenity spaces are proper nouns with a floor number attached — The Works on three, not 'state-of-the-art fitness center.' The register is understated confidence: state the fact and let it land. No exclamation points, no rhetorical questions, no 'imagine.' Banned words: luxury, world-class, bespoke, curated, elevated, resort-style, oasis, sanctuary, unparalleled, iconic, nestled. Section headlines run two to six words in sentence case; body copy never runs past three sentences before a break or a link. The same voice holds on the phone: warm, unhurried, factual. The leasing team quotes real residence numbers and exact rents, volunteers that advertised rents are net effective before being asked, never oversells the concession, and offers a tour as the next step rather than asking for a commitment.
paletteNotes: Warm bone paper against near-black graphite ink, with a single burnished-bronze accent used only for rules, small caps labels, and the primary CTA — never as a fill behind body text. #7F5E33 clears 4.5:1 on the paper for small text; #6E6B64 is for secondary and caption text only. Dark mode inverts to ink #12140F ground with paper as the type color and the bronze lightened to #C79A5E.
typographyNotes: Cormorant Garamond 300/400 for the wordmark, hero line, and section headers — set large, tight leading, generous letter-spacing on small caps. Jost 300/400/500 for all body copy, nav, tables, and the availability grid; its geometric structure reads like the Futura most NYC leasing collateral is set in. Both are on fonts.googleapis.com. Fallbacks: 'Cormorant Garamond', Georgia, serif and 'Jost', 'Helvetica Neue', Arial, sans-serif. Numerals in tables should be tabular.
leasingOffice: Leasing gallery on the ground floor, separate entrance on 5th Street. Two model residences open for tours. In-person, self-guided, and live video tours available; same-day appointments are usually possible.

buildingFacts.unitLines: A through L, no I line — eleven residences on a typical tower floor.
buildingFacts.podiumLines: M through T, no O line — seven additional lines that exist only on the podium floors, 5 through 9, where the plate is wider than the tower.
buildingFacts.residenceNumbering: Floor plus line letter — Residence 27C is line C on the 27th floor.

stack.note: The residential stack in three tiers, 5 through 33. 5 x 18 + 18 x 11 + 6 x 5 = 90 + 198 + 30 = 318.

tiers.name: Podium
tiers.lines: A through T, no I or O line
tiers.note: The base plate is wider than the tower, so these five floors carry seven lines the tower does not — M through T, no O. They are studios and one-bedrooms on the east and south faces and they are the building's Housing Connect inventory, which is why they are not part of the ten-plan market collection.

tiers.name: Tower
tiers.lines: A through L, no I line
tiers.note: The typical floor. Eleven residences, lines A through L with no I line, which is the stack the ten published plans are drawn on.

tiers.name: West Collection
tiers.note: Above the setback at 28 the plate narrows to five residences a floor — B3 on the B, C, and D lines, C2 on the A and E lines.

buildingFacts.affordableSetAside: 96 residences, 30 percent of 318, at 130% of area median income — the Option C set-aside under 421-a (Affordable New York). The tax exemption runs 35 years and the affordability restriction runs 40.
buildingFacts.affordableNote: 96 residences at 130% AMI were leased through NYC Housing Connect under the building's 421-a (Affordable New York) agreement: the 35 podium-line residences on floors 5 through 9, plus 61 residences distributed through the A-L stack in the same bedroom mix as the market residences. That inventory sits outside the market-rate funnel; the lottery closed in 2023 and the waitlist is administered by the city's designated marketing agent, not by the leasing office.
buildingFacts.prevailingWageNote: Two wage rules ride with the 421-a benefit. The Larkin sits in the Queens waterfront enhanced affordability area, so as a project of 300 or more residences it carried the 421-a construction wage requirement — a $45 minimum average hourly wage for construction workers, certified by an independent monitor. And because a 421-a building of 30 or more residences owes its building service employees the prevailing wage for the life of the exemption, the porters, doormen, and handypersons here are paid at the prevailing rate through the end of the exemption in 2058. Both costs sit in the operating budget; neither is billed to a resident.
buildingFacts.constructionNotes: Glass and champagne-anodized aluminum curtain wall over a two-story cast-stone base. The plate steps back twice: at 10, where the podium ends and the tower stack begins, and at 28, where the tower narrows to five residences a floor for the West Collection. The West Collection terraces are recessed into the D and A lines on all six floors, 28 through 33 — they are not a product of the setback, and no other line carries one.

team.leasing: Leased in-house by the Halbrook Residential on-site team. No broker fee.

concession.offer: One month free on a 14-month lease. No broker fee.
concession.disclosure: Advertised rents are net effective and reflect one month free on a 14-month lease. Gross rent is higher. Ask the leasing office for both figures.

policies.pets: Two pets per residence, 50 pounds each, dogs and cats. One-time non-refundable pet fee of $350 per pet; no monthly pet rent. Restricted breeds apply. Qualifying service animals and emotional support animals are exempt from pet fees and breed restrictions under New York law.
policies.application: Application fee $20 per adult, the New York State cap. Security deposit is one month's rent, the statutory maximum. Household income of 40x the monthly rent, or a guarantor at 80x who resides in NY, NJ, CT, or PA.
policies.leaseTerms: 12 to 24 months, priced by term. Shorter terms are quoted case by case and price at a premium.
policies.smoking: Smoke-free building, including terraces and all outdoor amenity space.
policies.movePolicy: Move-ins Monday through Saturday, 9am to 5pm, elevator reserved through the resident manager. $500 refundable move-in deposit.

sourceNote: DEMO PROPERTY — FICTIONAL. The Larkin does not exist. It was invented as the demo building for an AI leasing agent product so that a real property owner can browse a site and call the leasing line to test the assistant. The address (5-08 46th Avenue, Long Island City, NY 11101) is a plausible Queens hyphenated address on a real street grid but is not the address of any actual building; Halbrook Property Group, Halbrook Residential Management, Faircloth Rossi Architects, Studio Marlowe, and Bower & Field are invented entities. Rents, floor plans, availability, concessions, and occupancy are illustrative but calibrated to real 2026 Long Island City waterfront comps (The Orchard LIC, Jackson Park, Halo LIC) so the numbers survive a broker's sniff test. Neighborhood references — Gantry Plaza State Park, Casa Enrique, Sweetleaf, MoMA PS1, The Noguchi Museum, the 7 at Vernon Blvd-Jackson Ave, NYC Ferry at LIC Landing — are real places, used because a leasing conversation has to name real neighbors. The leasing phone number +1 (516) 990-9252 is the product's demo line. Nothing here should be presented as an actual rental offering.
